newsitem.title: FRANCE: French health spending fell 0.1 percent in Dec.
newsitem.headline: French health spending fell 0.1 percent in Dec.

text.p: French healthcare spending in December fell 0.1 percent from the previous month, health insurance fund Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie (CNAM) said on Tuesday.
For the full year, healthcare spending totalled 447.7 billion francs, up 3.3 percent from the previous year, and compared to a rise in 1995 of 4.7 percent, CNAM said in a statement.

The French government has introduced measures to curb healthcare spending to reduce France's big welfare deficit, as part of its drive to curb the total state deficit in preparation for European monetary union.
Government officials had said the spending curbs, brought in during the course of 1996, would start to show an impact towards the end of the year.
